about: Hook lab (Keith, 28 Nov 2026): the first 10 seconds of every episode are built from five parts. hooklab.py picks one level of each part for the next episode, scores every posted Reel, and keeps the formula in trends/hooklab.md. 7 x 3 x 4 x 3 x 7 = 1,764 different openings. Levels and examples were checked on 28 Nov 2026 against the hook study (research/hook-study-2026-11-28.md: 10 hook tutorials, 20 of the most-viewed finance shorts watched, 143 summarised). Since 28 Nov 2026 episodes are made in the turn format (see "format" and "formats"): hooklab.py pick chooses only from the levels that format can build.

goal.why: Keith: test openings until people are willing to watch to 10 seconds

priors.about: Each level's prior is a starting guess, in points of viewers still watching at 10 s against the average, from the hook study of 28 Nov 2026 and our own first 25 Reels. It weighs as much as one scored Reel, so real results overrule it within a few Reels. It also decides which untried level goes first.

cta.about: Keith, 28 Nov 2026: alternate the two CTA arms for about two weeks (even episodes K, odd O), then decide from trends/hooklab.md. When he picks, set arm to K or O. Paused the same day: the turn format has no CTA (arm N), so nothing alternates until "format" goes back to v3.

turn.about: Keith, 28 Nov 2026: every daily video is made in the turn format (SKILL.md §0): an odd thing from ordinary life, a jump to trading, the logic that joins them, an ending that is felt. No CTA. Its scene has no hook card and no big number, so the opening is picked from the levels below; lock is always turn.
turn.frame0: Keith, 28 Nov 2026, a hard rule (SKILL.md §0): the first frame, which is also the cover, shows the everyday place with people and "you" in it, so picture is place or action only. Episode 27 (object: a queue ticket that filled the frame for 1.6 s) lost 39.5% of viewers in the first 3 s; episode 26 (action: the whole supermarket, "you" changing lines) lost 24.9%. One Reel each: Keith's choice after seeing the frames side by side, not a test result.

v3.about: The story format (SKILL.md §1-4): one true money story that teaches a lesson, cheat-sheet CTA. Paused on 28 Nov 2026; set "format": "v3" to go back.

words.what: What the hook says: the card text (if there is a card) and the first spoken sentence. At most 14 spoken words, no date or name in front.

levels.how: Two facts that should not go together, the second on its own line.
levels.example: Card: They didn't sell. / Their *broker* did. Sentence: Taiwan lost 760 billion dollars in a week, and thousands never chose to sell.

levels.how: The money figure comes first: the card's first line starts with it and the sentence starts with it. Then the twist. Strongest with people or the viewer attached to the figure (how many people, whose money).
levels.example: Card: $25M in 12 seconds. / Then walked *free*. Sentence: 25 million dollars vanished in 12 seconds, and a judge said it wasn't theft.
levels.check: the first sentence has a number in its first 3 words

levels.how: The card is the question a normal person would ask on seeing the picture; the narrator asks it out loud, the way someone standing in the scene would. The answer must be something the viewer cannot guess.
levels.example: Card: How do you rob / an *offline* wallet? Sentence: How do you rob a wallet that has never been online?
levels.check: the first sentence ends with a question mark

levels.how: Name the viewer's own money. The card says who this is for; the sentence starts with If you or Your.
levels.example: Card: Own gold? / It just lost *a third*. Sentence: If you own gold, a third of its value is gone since January.
levels.check: you or your in the first sentence

levels.how: Cold open inside the moment: a time, a person, one action, present tense, at most 12 words. The size of the story lands in sentence 2.
levels.example: Card: Monday. 9 a.m. / One *email*. Sentence: Monday morning, an engineer opens a job offer.
levels.check: the first sentence has at most 12 words and no figure

levels.how: Put the viewer inside the story with a what-if that the true story answers. The sentence starts with If you, What if, Would you or How many; half a sentence is enough if sentence 2 finishes it. Sentence 2 lands the real event (It happened to ... this month).
levels.example: Card: Your bank app / says *$0*. Sentence: What if you opened your bank app tomorrow, and it said zero? (Then: It happened to three million people in Paraguay this month.)
levels.check: the first sentence starts with If, What if, Would you, Could you, How many or How long
levels.why: hook study 28 Nov 2026 (research/hook-study-2026-11-28.md): three of the animated finance shorts with 3.7-6.1M views open on an If you / How many times would you line

levels.how: Someone or something unnamed did what should not be possible; the name comes in the lock-in at the earliest, or is the question of the whole video. Card and sentence start with Someone, Nobody, One man, One email, A stranger. Sourced facts only; an allegation keeps its says / is accused.
levels.example: Card: Someone made / *$350M* in a day. Sentence: Someone turned three million dollars into 350 million in one afternoon.
levels.check: the first sentence names nobody (no proper name)
levels.why: hook study 28 Nov 2026 (research/hook-study-2026-11-28.md): a 17-second Reel built on an unnamed someone reached 7.4M

text.what: What is written on the first frame (it is also the cover).

levels.how: The big two-line hook card at y 640 from frame 0 (HOOK and HOOK_SUB in script.py).
No card. Leave HOOK out: the first sentence shows as word-by-word captions from frame 0, like the rest of the video. HOOK_SUB shows as a small chip (subject and date).

A headline box at the top from frame 0 to the last frame. HOOK (2 lines, 10 words at most, one *amber* word) says the topic and the tension; HOOK_SUB is the small tag above it (place and date, or TRUE STORY). The first sentence runs as captions under it from frame 0. The engine moves captions, chips and name cards down by SH (160 px): place your own top labels with put() as usual.
levels.example: HOOK = ["3 million people", "locked out of their *money*"], HOOK_SUB = "Paraguay · Nov 2026"
levels.check: qa.py: the banner is on the first frame and still there near the end
levels.why: hook study 28 Nov 2026 (research/hook-study-2026-11-28.md): 12 of the 20 most-viewed finance shorts we watched keep a headline on screen for the whole video

picture.what: What the camera shows from frame 0 to 1.5 s. Whatever the level, something moves in the first half second.

levels.how: A wide shot of the story's main place, slowly pushing in.

The main event is already happening on frame 0, in the middle of the frame: coins pour out, a crowd runs, lights go out floor by floor, a line falls. Start mid-move and let the camera move with it. At least a third of the frame is moving.
levels.check: qa.py measures the change between frame 0 and frame 30

levels.how: One large bright object fills at least half the frame height (a pile of gold, a vault door, a giant coin, a wallet). Best when the number is written on the object itself (a banknote, a price tag, a cheque, a screen). Camera close, slowly circling; the place is only background.
One figure close to the camera, at least a third of the frame height, doing what the sentence says (on a phone, at a desk, on a call screen). Never a real person's likeness.
The big number counts up over a darkened screen (BIG in script.py).
The same big number, but the world stays bright and keeps moving behind it; the number sits on a small dark plate (BIG in script.py).

No number card (leave BIG out). At 1.5 s a second thing happens in the world that shows how big the story is: the price board crashes, the crowd doubles, the gold is gone. Name the cue T.beat2 in scene.js.

lock.what: The lock-in, 3-10 s (sentences 2-3): why the rest is worth watching. It ends on the question the video answers.

levels.how: How big it is (the record, the comparison), then the question.
levels.example: It's the biggest crypto theft on record. So how does one interview empty an exchange?

levels.how: Say what the viewer will take away for their own money, then the question.
levels.example: And it shows the one number every index-fund owner should check. So how can one stock drag down 500?

levels.how: Name what most people believe, then turn it over.
levels.example: Most people think a wallet that's never online can't be robbed. This one was. So how?

levels.how: Give the mechanism a short name the viewer will want explained.
levels.example: Traders call it a margin call, and it decides when you sell. So who was calling?

levels.how: Promise one concrete payoff with a number, then the question.
levels.example: Stay to the end and you'll see how a thousand dollars became 55 million. So how does one man end up with that much to give?

levels.how: Turn the story onto the viewer in one line with one small number of their own (their savings, their salary, their coffee): If you had ..., or What that means for you is ... Then the question.
levels.example: If you'd had a thousand dollars in that bank, you'd be locked out tonight. So how does a whole bank freeze?
levels.why: hook study 28 Nov 2026 (research/hook-study-2026-11-28.md): the news shorts with 8M+ views say what it means for the viewer inside the first 15 seconds

levels.how: Say that the strangest part is still to come and name its kind without giving it (that's not even the strange part / there's one catch / and it isn't the biggest one), then the question. Never pay it off before the second half.
levels.example: And the theft isn't even the strange part. So who walked away with the money?
levels.why: hook study 28 Nov 2026 (research/hook-study-2026-11-28.md): 'we are not even close to the largest one', 'there's one catch'

levels.how: Turn format only. One short sentence that jumps from the everyday thing to trading or money and speaks to the viewer, starting by 8 s (aim for 4-6 s), then a short bridge into the reason (Here's why.). No explanation inside the turn: it should make no sense yet.
levels.example: You do the same thing when you trade. Here's why.
levels.check: tts.sh: the lock-in names trading or money and starts by 8 s
levels.why: Keith, 28 Nov 2026, after the Reel instagram.com/reel/DgMKBJJMeMP; first built in episode 26

ideas.note: Levels to add when one is retired (trends/hooklab.md lists retire candidates). Add the new level here with since = today and a clear how; never reuse an id.
words: record: the biggest / first / worst ever, said plainly
versus: two sides, one question (X vs Y)
clock: how fast it happened (In 12 seconds...)
quote: one short line someone in the story said, attributed
line: a character in the scene says the first line (needs a second voice: ask Keith first)
names: two short parallel facts with names everybody knows, then 'it's worth asking why'
text: word: one giant word (ROBBED) instead of a sentence
board: a live scoreboard from frame 0 (two or three numbers that change during the video)
labels: two labels for a split screen (THEN / NOW, A / B)
picture: fall: the camera drops from the sky into the scene
chart: a 3D chart line as a cliff with one small figure at the edge
split: before and after side by side
hand: a giant hand holding or taking the object
count: rows of small figures, most of them greyed out
split2: the same start, two paths side by side with running numbers
proof: the proof picture of the story on frame 0 (the stamp, the three coins)
beat2: counter: the number counts in a corner while the action goes on
compare: two numbers, before and after
rows: 9 of every 10 figures fall over
count0: the number is already counting on frame 0 on a small plate, no dark screen
lock: test: ask the viewer what they would have done
list: three things had to go wrong
who: name who paid for it
catch: 'There's one catch.' then the rule that changes everything
acted: act the madness out in one or two quoted lines, then 'Think that's a joke?'
